This shift in sentiment often occurs when traders anticipate changes in monetary policy, such as a pause or slowdown in interest rate hikes by major central banks like the US Federal Reserve, which could make the yen relatively more attractive.

source_item.title: U.S. 10-year yield briefly breaks 5% for first time since 2024 after Aug CPI

card.plain_headline: US 10-year Treasury yield tops 5% after CPI data
card.what_happened: The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note briefly surpassed 5% for the first time since 2024, following the release of August Consumer Price Index (CPI) data. Higher yields indicate that investors are demanding more return for holding US government debt, often due to inflation concerns or expectations of higher interest rates.
card.what_happened_verbose: The interest rate, or yield, on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury bond briefly climbed above 5% for the first time since the year 2024. This significant level was breached shortly after the release of the August Consumer Price Index (CPI) report, which measures inflation. When yields rise, it means the price of existing bonds is falling. This event suggests that investors are concerned about inflation or anticipate that the Federal Reserve will need to keep interest rates higher for longer to combat it, making new bonds with higher yields more attractive.
